title: Firewall failover leaves routing asymmetric; long-lived flows get reset
source_note: Failure pattern (a network appliance failover that leaves outbound and return traffic on different paths, so stateful firewalls drop the 'unseen-direction' packets and connections needing many round-trips fail while short ones succeed) is a classic asymmetric-routing incident. All services, log lines, metrics, and timestamps are fabricated for evaluation.
incident_report: Since ~09:19 UTC large file uploads and streaming responses are failing about 40% of the time with connection resets. Small quick requests mostly work. No deploys. Network team did a planned firewall failover this morning.

signal_lines.msg: planned failover of the edge firewall pair to the secondary unit completed
elevated connection resets on long-lived flows; short requests mostly OK
large uploads and streaming responses failing ~40%; TCP resets mid-transfer
packet capture: return traffic routes via the primary firewall while outbound uses the secondary - asymmetric path; stateful inspection drops return packets
corrected the return route to match outbound; failing flows recovering

ground_truth.root_cause: A planned failover of the edge firewall pair to the secondary unit created an asymmetric network path: outbound traffic went through the secondary firewall while return traffic still routed through the primary. Each stateful firewall only saw one direction of a connection, so it dropped the 'unexpected' return packets. Connections needing many round-trips (large uploads, streaming responses) failed with mid-transfer TCP resets at ~40%, while short request/response pairs usually completed before hitting the problem. The trigger is the failover leaving routing asymmetric. Recovery required correcting the return route to match the outbound path.
evidence_path: network-ops INFO at 09:15: planned failover of the edge firewall pair to the secondary completed
region-gateway WARN: elevated connection resets on long-lived flows while short requests are mostly fine
large uploads and streaming responses fail ~40% with mid-transfer TCP resets
packet capture shows return traffic via the primary firewall and outbound via the secondary - an asymmetric path; stateful inspection drops the return packets
recovery after the return route is corrected to match outbound
ground_truth.fix: Correct the return route so both directions traverse the same firewall (done). Make firewall failover switch both directions atomically, add a post-failover synthetic check for large-transfer and long-lived connections, and enable stateful-session sync between the firewall pair.
